format.melody: Bars separated by |. A note is letter + optional # or b (## / bb) + octave + duration (w h q e s = whole, half, quarter, eighth, sixteenth), then optional . (dotted) and ~ (tied to the next note of the same pitch). r + duration is a rest. Middle C is C4. Accidentals are the sounding pitch, not relative to the key signature. If the tune has a pickup, the first bar holds only the pickup beats.
format.chords: One entry per full bar (no chord for the pickup), separated by |. Several chords in a bar split it evenly, or give beats with Chord:beats. Qualities: (major) m 7 m7 maj7 dim dim7 m7b5 6 m6 aug sus4 9.
format.band: Default play-along style: swing, twobeat, rock, bossa, ballad (4/4); waltz, jazzwaltz, ballad (3/4).

tunes.title: Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star
tunes.composer: French folk melody (“Ah! vous dirai-je, maman”)
tunes.year: Melody printed 1761 · words by Jane Taylor, 1806

tunes.chords: C | F C | F C | G7 C | C F | C G | C F | C G | C | F C | F C | G7 C
tunes.about: Mozart wrote twelve variations on this melody (K. 265). Do what he did: keep the chords and change the tune.
tunes.source: Melody as printed in Paris, 1761; public domain everywhere. Chords added for this page.

tunes.title: Frère Jacques
tunes.melody: F4q G4q A4q F4q | F4q G4q A4q F4q | A4q Bb4q C5h | A4q Bb4q C5h | C5e D5e C5e Bb4e A4q F4q | C5e D5e C5e Bb4e A4q F4q | F4q C4q F4h | F4q C4q F4h
tunes.about: A round: a second group starts the same tune two bars later and it still fits. Mahler turned it into a slow minor-key march in his First Symphony (1888). Try “Upside down” for a melody that sounds almost as natural.
tunes.source: Traditional; public domain. Chords added for this page.

D4e D4h | E4q E4q F#4q D4q | E4q F#4e G4e F#4q D4q | E4q F#4e G4e F#4q E4q | D4q E4q A3h | F#4q F#4q G4q A4q | A4q G4q F#4q E4q | D4q D4q E4q F#4q | E4q. D4e D4h
tunes.about: Beethoven’s tune moves almost entirely by step, one scale note at a time. Try “Chord tones” and “Skeleton” to hear the harmony underneath it.
tunes.source: Beethoven, Symphony No. 9, Op. 125 (1824), in its original key of D; public domain. Chords simplified for this page.

tunes.title: When the Saints Go Marching In
tunes.year: Printed by 1896 · a New Orleans jazz standard
tunes.melody: C4q E4q F4q | G4w | r4q C4q E4q F4q | G4w | r4q C4q E4q F4q | G4h E4h | C4h E4h | D4w | r4q E4q E4q D4q | C4h. C4q | E4h G4h | G4h F4h | r4h E4q F4q | G4h E4h | C4h D4h | C4w | r4w
tunes.chords: C | C | C | C | C | C | G7 | G7 | C | C7 | F | F | C | C:2 G7:2 | C | C
tunes.about: Starts with a three-note pickup before bar 1. New Orleans bands play it in a “two-beat” feel: bass on 1 and 3, snare on 2 and 4. Switch the band to Swing and play with “Push” to hear it get jazzier.
tunes.source: Traditional spiritual; public domain. Lead sheet written for this page from the traditional melody.

tunes.title: Amazing Grace
tunes.year: Tune printed 1829 · words by John Newton, 1779
tunes.melody: D4q | G4h B4e G4e | B4h A4q | G4h E4q | D4h D4q | G4h B4e G4e | B4h A4q | D5h.~ | D5h B4q | D5h B4e G4e | B4h A4q | G4h E4q | D4h D4q | G4h B4e G4e | B4h A4q | G4h.~ | G4h r4q
tunes.chords: G | G7 | C | G | G | D | D | G | G | G7 | C | G | Em | D7 | G | G
tunes.about: In 3/4 time with a one-beat pickup. The melody uses only five notes of the scale (a pentatonic scale), which is why it works on so many instruments. Try the Jazz waltz band.
tunes.source: “New Britain” as printed in Columbian Harmony (1829); public domain. Chords added for this page.

tunes.title: Greensleeves
tunes.melody: A4q | C5h D5q | E5q. F5e E5q | D5h B4q | G4q. A4e B4q | C5h A4q | A4q. G#4e A4q | B4h G#4q | E4h A4q | C5h D5q | E5q. F5e E5q | D5h B4q | G4q. A4e B4q | C5q. B4e A4q | G#4q. F#4e G#4q | A4h. | A4h r4q
tunes.chords: Am | C | G | Em | Am | F:1 E:2 | E | E | Am | C | G | Em | Am | E | Am | Am
tunes.about: A minor key. The G♯ is borrowed from the harmonic minor scale to lead back to A. The same tune became the carol “What Child Is This?” (1865).
tunes.source: Traditional English tune; public domain. Lead sheet and chords written for this page.

tunes.title: Auld Lang Syne
tunes.year: Words by Robert Burns, 1788 · tune printed 1799
tunes.melody: C4q | F4q. F4e F4q A4q | G4q. F4e G4q A4q | F4q. F4e A4q C5q | D5h. D5q | C5q. A4e A4q F4q | G4q. F4e G4q A4e G4e | F4q. D4e D4q C4q | F4h. r4q
tunes.chords: F | C7 | F | Bb | F | C7 | Dm:2 Bb:1 C7:1 | F
tunes.about: Only five notes: F G A C D, the major pentatonic scale. The dotted “long-short” rhythm is a Scottish fingerprint. Try “Short-long” to hear the Scotch snap.
tunes.source: Traditional Scottish tune; public domain. Verse only. Chords added for this page.

tunes.title: Classroom Blues
tunes.composer: Original riff for ClassroomOS (free to use)
tunes.melody: C4e Eb4e E4q G4q r4q | A4q G4e Eb4e C4q r4q | r4q C5q Bb4q G4q | C5h r4h | F4e Ab4e A4q C5q r4q | D5q C5e Ab4e F4q r4q | C4e Eb4e E4q G4q r4q | A4q G4e Eb4e C4q r4q | G4e Bb4e B4q D5q r4q | F4e Ab4e A4q C5q r4q | C4e Eb4e E4q G4q r4q | r4q G4q F4q D4q
tunes.about: The 12-bar blues: four bars on I, two on IV, two on I, then V, IV, I, V. The riff moves to fit each chord. Use Trade fours to improvise your own riff in the empty bars.
tunes.source: Written for this site; free for any classroom to copy, play and change.
